name: Chemistry and physics of life
desc: Energy, water, weak forces and the molecules they shape.

decks.title: Energy and Redox
decks.sub: Where a cell’s energy comes from
decks.blurb: Free energy, coupling, redox potentials and an interactive electron tower; syntrophy on thin margins.

decks.title: Water, pH and Scale
decks.sub: Life in water, at the scale of a micrometre
decks.blurb: Buffers and pKa, pH homeostasis, water activity, turgor, diffusion, Reynolds number and surface-to-volume.

decks.title: The Molecules of Life
decks.blurb: Weak interactions, folding and domains, base pairing and supercoiling, bilayers and glycosidic linkages.

decks.title: Enzyme Kinetics
decks.sub: How enzymes work, and how fast
decks.blurb: Catalysis, Michaelis–Menten, inhibition, cooperativity and allostery, and kinetics in antibiotic action.

decks.title: Glycans and Glycosyltransferases
decks.sub: Sugars, and the enzymes that join them
decks.blurb: Monosaccharides, linkages and nucleotide sugars; glycosyltransferase folds and mechanisms; and how the pneumococcal capsule is built.

name: The central dogma
desc: Copying DNA, reading it, making and placing proteins, and repairing the genome.

decks.title: How DNA Is Copied
decks.sub: Every cell copies its DNA before it divides
decks.blurb: From Meselson–Stahl and Kornberg to the bacterial replisome, with a mutant explorer.

decks.title: How Genes Are Transcribed
decks.blurb: RNA polymerase, sigma factors, termination and regulation in bacteria, with eukaryotic comparisons.

decks.title: How Proteins Are Made
decks.blurb: Proteins, tRNA, the ribosome, the genetic code, and the antibiotics that jam translation.

decks.title: Protein Targeting and Modification
decks.sub: After the ribosome: sending and finishing proteins
decks.blurb: Signal peptides, Sec and Tat, SRP, YidC, envelope assembly, secretion systems and glycosylation.

decks.title: Repairing DNA
decks.blurb: Damage, direct reversal, excision and mismatch repair, recombination, SOS and translesion synthesis.

decks.title: Cell Envelopes
decks.sub: The layers that hold a microbe together
decks.blurb: Gram-positive, Gram-negative and acid-fast envelopes, peptidoglycan, LPS, teichoic and mycolic acids, archaeal membranes.

decks.title: Organelles and Endosymbiosis
decks.blurb: Organelles, the secretory and endocytic pathways, pathogens that hijack them, and the bacterial origin of mitochondria and plastids.

decks.title: How Bacteria Divide
decks.blurb: The fts genes, Z ring, Min and nucleoid occlusion, MapZ, the septal wall, and drugs that stop division.

decks.title: Motility and Chemotaxis
decks.sub: How bacteria move, and decide where to go
decks.blurb: The flagellar motor, runs and tumbles, the chemotaxis circuit and its adaptation, pili and gliding.

name: Regulation
desc: How a bacterial gene is built, and how cells decide which genes to use.

decks.title: Anatomy of a Prokaryotic Gene
decks.blurb: Promoter to terminator, operons, and the causes of polar effects, including overexpression and antisense from cassettes.

decks.title: Bacterial Gene Regulation
decks.sub: How a cell decides which genes to use
decks.blurb: Operons and regulons, lac, two-component systems, small RNAs, quorum sensing, sporulation, phase variation and persisters.

name: Genetics and genomes
desc: Inheritance, evolution, mobile DNA and genome biology.

decks.title: Bateson's Epistasis
decks.blurb: Bateson’s sweet-pea crosses, the 9:7 ratio, and the main kinds of epistasis.

decks.title: Mutation, Selection and Drift
decks.blurb: Mutation rates, drift, selection, recombination, the long-term evolution experiment, epistasis, clonal interference and the cost of resistance.

decks.title: Mobile DNA and Plasmids
decks.blurb: Transformation, conjugation and transduction; transposons, integrons and ICEs; plasmid replication, incompatibility and addiction.

decks.title: Phages and Defences
decks.sub: Bacteriophages, and how bacteria fight them
decks.blurb: Lytic and temperate cycles, the λ decision, restriction–modification and the anti-phage arsenal, coevolution and phage therapy.

decks.title: Bacterial Genomes
decks.sub: How a bacterial genome is laid out
decks.blurb: Size and density, organisation around replication, GC skew, codon usage, genome decay and pangenomes.

name: Metabolism
desc: Carbon, energy and the element cycles.

decks.title: Central Carbon Metabolism
decks.sub: Sugar to precursors, energy and reducing power
decks.blurb: EMP, ED and pentose phosphate pathways, precursor metabolites, the TCA cycle, anaplerosis, overflow and catabolite repression.

decks.title: Respiration and Fermentation
decks.sub: Making ATP with and without an acceptor
decks.blurb: Chemiosmosis, ATP synthase, branched respiratory chains, alternative acceptors and fermentation end products.

decks.title: Autotrophy and the Element Cycles
decks.sub: Fixing carbon and nitrogen, cycling the rest
decks.blurb: Six ways to fix CO₂, phototrophy, nitrogen fixation and the N, S and methane cycles, and who runs each step.

name: Tools
desc: Building, editing and screening DNA in the lab.

decks.title: Tools for Molecular Cloning
decks.blurb: Restriction cloning to Golden Gate, MoClo and Gibson; recombineering and allelic exchange.

decks.title: How CRISPR–Cas9 Works
decks.sub: An immune system with a memory
decks.blurb: CRISPR as bacterial immunity, how Cas9 finds and cuts DNA, and how it became a genome-editing tool.

decks.title: Next-Generation Sequencing
decks.sub: Reading DNA a billion molecules at a time
decks.blurb: Sanger to nanopore: how each platform holds molecules apart and detects a base, what each gets wrong, and which to choose for a given job.

decks.title: How Tn-seq Works
decks.sub: Finding the genes a cell can’t live without
decks.blurb: Transposon libraries, sequencing insertion sites, and calling essential genes.

name: History
desc: Classic experiments, and the logic that made them decisive.

decks.title: Pasteur and the Swan-Neck Flask
decks.blurb: Spontaneous generation and the swan-neck flask, hay infusions and spores, fermentation, and the first controlled vaccine trial.

decks.title: Koch and the Pure Culture
decks.blurb: Anthrax and serial passage, solid media and pure culture, tuberculosis, and the postulates tested against real diseases.

decks.title: Winogradsky and the Soil
decks.blurb: Energy from sulfur and ammonia, nitrifiers on silica gel, elective culture, and the Winogradsky column.

decks.title: Beijerinck and the First Virus
decks.blurb: Tobacco mosaic and the first virus, enrichment culture, nitrogen fixers, and the Delft school.

decks.title: Griffith, Avery and DNA
decks.blurb: Pneumococcal types, Griffith’s mice, purifying the transforming principle, and the enzyme test that pointed to DNA.

decks.title: Lederberg and Bacterial Genetics
decks.blurb: The fluctuation test, bacterial mating, replica plating and transduction.

decks.title: Woese and the Tree of Life
decks.blurb: 16S rRNA as a molecular clock, oligonucleotide catalogues, the archaea, and the three domains.
